example:
d = Node("d")
b = Node("b", d)
a = Node("a", b, Node("c"))
lowest_common_ancestor(a, d, b)
start: Picture folders: `a` holds `b` and `c`, and `b` holds `d`. For `d` and `b` the answer is `b`, since a folder counts as containing itself. For `d` and a node that is not in the tree the answer is `None`, even though you found `d`: finding one of them proves nothing about the other.

Work bottom up, children before parents: each subtree reports a mask of what it contains (1 for `p`, 2 for `q`, 3 for both, matched with `is`) and its answer, if it has one. A node combines its children's masks with its own matches using `|`, and the first node to reach 3 with no answer from below becomes the answer. A parent passes a lower answer up unchanged, and a root mask below 3 means `None`.

start.text: The tests walk a 5,000-node chain, so use an explicit stack and put each node on it twice: once to push its children, and once, after they are done, to combine their reports. The shape:

test_identity_presence_and_depth: Every node holds `7`, so only `is` tells them apart. With `a` over `b` and `c`, and `d` under `b`: `(d, b)` gives `b`, `(d, c)` gives `a`, `(d, d)` gives `d`, and `(d, Node(7))` gives `None`, since that new node is not in the tree. Returning the first of `p` or `q` you meet answers `d` there.

An empty tree gives `None`. Then a 5,000-node chain of `right` children asks about `nodes[123]` and the last node, answer `nodes[123]`: a recursive walk stops at Python's recursion limit of about 1,000 calls long before the bottom.
test_invalid_structure_even_when_answer_: Each root is queried with `p` as both nodes: a node with `p` as both children, a node with `p` on the left and `42` on the right, a node whose `right` is itself, and `42`. All four must raise `ValueError`, although `p` is found on the left in the first two. Check every node, not just until the answer is known, and keep a set of the nodes you have entered: one met twice is a shared child or a loop.
`lowest_common_ancestor(p, None, p)` must raise `ValueError` as well: check that `p` and `q` are both `Node` objects before walking.
test_root_path_oracle: 50 random trees of 1 to 24 nodes, all holding `7`, with 30 random `(p, q)` pairs each, drawn from the tree's nodes plus one node outside it. Some pairs are one node twice, some have one node above the other, and a pair with the outside node must give `None`. The expected answer is the last node shared by the two root-to-node paths.

RecursionError: “Identity presence and depth” ends with a 5,000-node chain, and Python stops recursion at about 1,000 calls. Use an explicit stack and handle each node twice: first to push its children, then, once they are done, to combine their reports.
In “Invalid structure even when answer seems known” it can mean a walk went round the node whose `right` is itself. Keep a set of the nodes you have entered and raise `ValueError` on a repeat.
AttributeError: You read `.left` or `.right` on `42`: “Invalid structure even when answer seems known” uses it as a right child and as the root. Check `isinstance(node, Node)` on every node you step onto, and raise `ValueError`.
KeyError: A dict of subtree reports read with `report[node.left]` fails when that child is missing: `None` never got a report. Give a missing side a default, nothing found and no answer, with `.get`.

stopped: A stack loop that never ends is going round the node whose `right` is itself, in “Invalid structure even when answer seems known”. Keep a set of the nodes you have entered, and raise `ValueError` on a repeat before pushing its children.
If each node goes on the stack twice, the second push must be marked as done. A frame that pushes its children every time it comes off the stack refills the stack forever.
passing: All passing. Time a chain of 100,000 `right` children as your own input, with `p` near the top and `q` at the bottom. Then the README's second follow-up: if one unchanged tree must answer thousands of queries, what would you compute once so that each query costs less than a full walk?
